A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DMS and QDDM research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and can be reliably matched despite reformatting and section relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations across nine benchmark settings and three QDDM settings, including repeated trials, statistical comparisons, and ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results, including the main comparisons, appendix ablations, and generated-image examples.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, the discount-model target in Equation 1, CMA-ES emitters, empty-point training, and archive updates are unchanged. The documented MLP architectures and CLIP embedding procedure also remain the same.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same eight Linear Projection variants, Arm Repertoire, triangle arrangement with MNIST and Fashion-MNIST, and LSI (Hiker) with LHQ256. No evaluated dataset, task, or scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership remains CMA-MAE, DDS, MAP-Elites (line), and MAP-Elites in the benchmarks, with DDS excluded from QDDM experiments in both versions. Differentiable QD methods remain discussed but unevaluated.

E3.justification: The evaluation metrics, 10,000-iteration budget, matched solution-evaluation counts, archive configurations, and Table 6 hyperparameters are unchanged. The appendix domain descriptions retain the same preprocessing and objectives.

E4.justification: The archive-learning-rate, empty-point, and restart-rule ablations in v1 Appendix C are retained in v3 Appendix D with identical evidence. Distortion diagnostics, archive visualizations, and generated-image examples also remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both report 20 trials for benchmark experiments and five for QDDM experiments, means and standard errors, and the same Levene, Welch ANOVA, and Games-Howell testing procedures. Appendix uncertainty reporting is retained.

E6.justification: Matched performance, ablation, statistical-comparison, and detailed runtime tables are identical. For example, DMS retains a QD Score of 6,409.50 and 89.21% coverage in 10D LP (Sphere). The runtime results move from v1 Table 5 to v3 Table 2.

T1.justification: The QD formulation, discount-target equation, domain equations, and manifold assumption are unchanged. No theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: smooth discount models improve exploration, DMS outperforms existing black-box comparators in the reported settings, and QDDM enables specifying desired measures through datasets.

C2.justification: The new Ethics Statement identifies possible amplification of biases in measure datasets, generators, and distance metrics, alongside artist-style mimicry, and suggests mitigations. Existing result interpretations, mechanism explanations, and technical limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 adds a project-page link and explicitly identifies README instructions for environment setup and experiment reproduction; the code repository was already linked in v1. It also replaces approximate runtime summaries with a reference to the retained detailed timing table.

R1.justification: v3 adds Maluleke et al. (2022), Perera and Patel (2023), Shan et al. (2023), and Tseng et al. (2021) for the ethics discussion. The existing QD and latent-space research positioning is preserved in the relocated Related Work section.

P1.justification: Most prose remains essentially unchanged. Related Work moves from Section 8 to Appendix A; Ethics and Reproducibility statements are added, runtime prose is shortened, and limited abstract, terminology, citation-style, and author/header edits are made.

P2.justification: The ACM format with two-column main text becomes an ICLR single-column document, substantially changing typography, margins, figure scaling, and placement. The runtime table moves into the main text, and appendix displays are redistributed, while their underlying content is retained.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves transparency through specific societal-impact caveats and clearer reproduction directions. Moving the existing runtime table into the main text also makes computational costs easier to assess. These are limited documentation gains; the method, experimental evidence, and technical limitations remain unchanged.
